messages.author: 14cad522d99ed9fa
messages.subject: Speed up questions
parts:
These questions are straight from the FAQ, so apologies in advance if there's an obvious answer. I'm trying to implement some of the suggestions in the "How can I speed up my code?" section of the FAQ, but running into issues.

Consider the following toy rstan example:

################################
n = 10
d = 3
m = 2

t1 = matrix(rnorm(n*m),n,m)
t2 = matrix(rnorm(m*d),m,d)
x = t1%*%t2
datalist = list(n=n,d=d,x=x,m=m)

code <- '   
  data {
    int<lower=1> n; 
    int<lower=1> d; 
    int<lower=1> m; 
    real x[n,d]; 
  }   
  parameters {
    real alpha[n,m]; 
    real beta[m,d];
  }
  model {
    real S[n,d];
    alpha ~ normal(0,1);
    beta ~ normal(0,1);

    S <- alpha * beta;

    for (i in 1:n)
      for (j in 1:d)
        x[i,j] ~ normal(S[i,j],1)
  }
'  


fit <- stan(model_code = code, data = datalist, 
       iter = 400, warmup = 100, chains = 1)
################################

There are two issues here. First, I cannot apply the normal prior to the parameter matrices alpha and beta. I get this:
DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
no matches for function name="normal_log"
    arg 0 type=real[2]
    arg 1 type=int
    arg 2 type=int
available function signatures for normal_log:
0.  normal_log(real, real, real) : real
[truncated]

However, it works just fine if I replace it with the (presumably) slower version: 
######
    for (i in 1:n)
      for (j in 1:d)
        alpha[i,j] ~ normal(0,1);
######
 

Second, the matrix multiplication does not seem to want to work. The "S <- alpha * beta;" line gives me this:
DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
no matches for function name="multiply"
    arg 0 type=real[2]
    arg 1 type=real[2]
available function signatures for multiply:
0.  multiply(real, real) : real
[truncated]

Again, replacing it with the slower scalar operation version works just fine.

Any idea what my problems are? Thanks

We've only vectorized one level deep. So you can have
1D arrays, but not matrices. So what would work is this:

for (n in 1:n)
alpha[n] ~ normal(0,1);

> Second, the matrix multiplication does not seem to want to work. The "S <- alpha * beta;" line gives me this:
> DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
> no matches for function name="multiply"
> arg 0 type=real[2]
> arg 1 type=real[2]
> available function signatures for multiply:
> 0. multiply(real, real) : real
> [truncated]
>
> Again, replacing it with the slower scalar operation version works just fine.
>
> Any idea what my problems are? Thanks

Here you're trying to plug a 2D array into a matrix operation.
Declare them as:

parameters {
matrix[n,m] alpha;
matrix[m,d] beta;
}

and the multiplication should do what you expect. And similarly
declare S as an (n x d) matrix.

- Bob
